title: Where distributed PostgreSQL work runs
brief: Choose where PostgreSQL-distributed work runs from co-location, constraint scope and movement requirements.
outcomes: Distinguish native partitions, application shards, Citus and foreign tables
Derive local work, skew and a safe ownership transfer
entry: General sharding, distributed transactions and PostgreSQL architecture.

heading.title: Four placement choices
heading.brief: Compare one-server partitions, application routing, Citus and foreign tables by who owns execution, consistency and failure recovery; avoid treating FDWs as a distributed transaction guarantee.

heading.title: Co-location and constraints
heading.brief: Use shop_id to place related tables together; verify distributed unique and foreign-key restrictions for the pinned Citus release.

heading.title: Cross-shard work
heading.brief: Follow an order report and a global quota through coordinator and workers; expose fan-out, reference data, skew and transaction scope.

heading.title: Moving an owner
heading.brief: Explain snapshot, catch-up, fenced route switch and validation for the chosen method; verify extension/version support and recovery obligations before suggesting live movement.
